new.title: Gaze at the carved portal of the Gök Medrese
new.desc: The Gök (Blue) Medrese was built in 1271 by the Seljuk vizier Sahib Ata Fahreddin Ali and is famed for its marble-and-tile portal and twin brick minarets. It now houses a foundation museum and is one of the emblems of Sivas.
new.tip: Go in daylight when the portal is well lit; the courtyard museum is small. It sits at the foot of the old citadel, a short walk from the main square.
new.q: Gök Medrese, Kale Mahallesi, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: See the twin minarets of the Çifte Minareli Medrese
new.desc: Built in 1271-72 for the Ilkhanid vizier Shams al-Din Juvayni, this medrese kept only its monumental brick-and-tile portal and the two fluted minarets that became the symbol of Sivas. Its entrance facade is among the finest examples of Anatolian Seljuk stonework.
new.tip: Free to see from the square; late afternoon gives the best light for photos.
new.q: Çifte Minareli Medrese, Kale Mahallesi, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Walk the courtyard of the Buruciye Medrese
new.desc: Founded in 1271 by Muzaffar al-Burujirdi, the Buruciye Medrese is a symmetrically planned Seljuk teaching school with a celebrated crown gate. Its arcaded courtyard is one of the best preserved in the city.
new.tip: Used as a cultural centre with a tea garden in the courtyard; pair it with the neighbouring medreses on Kent Meydanı.
new.q: Buruciye Medresesi, Kent Meydanı, Eskikale, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Step inside the 12th-century Sivas Ulu Cami
new.desc: Dated to 1197, the Ulu Cami is the oldest major building in Sivas and one of the oldest mosques in Anatolia, with a forest of columns in a flat-roofed prayer hall. Its brick minaret is attributed to Sultan Kaykaus I.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly. It stands just off the main square.
new.q: Sivas Ulu Camii, Cemal Gürsel Caddesi, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Walk through the Sivas Congress building
new.desc: This Ottoman school of 1892 hosted the Sivas Congress of 4-12 September 1919, a milestone of the Turkish National Struggle. It opened as a museum in 1990 and now holds the Atatürk and Congress Museum upstairs and ethnography halls below.
new.tip: Entry has been reported free; allow an hour and check opening hours after the recent restoration.
new.q: Atatürk ve Kongre Müzesi, Sivas Lisesi, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Watch craftsmen at the Sanayi Mektebi living museum
new.desc: Housed in the old Hamidiye industrial school, this museum runs as a living museum with working craft workshops and a craftsmen's bazaar. It reported over 25,000 visitors in its first six months.
new.tip: Come in the morning when the workshops are active; a good place for local souvenirs.
new.q: Sanayi Mektebi, Eskikale, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Admire the lion-ringed Behrampaşa Han
new.desc: Completed in 1573 (some sources say 1576), the Behrampaşa Han was the first lodging for travellers entering Sivas from the south and has lion motifs around its windows. It was restored after years of ruin and now operates as a hotel with a café.
new.tip: Non-guests can usually sit in the courtyard café; ask at reception.
new.q: Behram Paşa Hanı, Eskikale, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Trace railway history at the Cer Atölyeleri museum
new.desc: Founded in 1939 to repair steam locomotives and freight wagons, the Sivas Cer Workshops (now TÜDEMSAŞ) keep a museum of about 3,000 railway objects, including a rail from 1889 and Ottoman-era tools. It reflects the role of Sivas as a railway town.
new.tip: Visits normally need advance arrangement with TÜDEMSAŞ; confirm before going.
new.q: TÜDEMSAŞ, Cer Atölyeleri, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Browse fossils and Hittite finds at Sivas Archaeological Museum
new.desc: Set in a former factory building of 1914, the museum shows finds from the Hittite, Roman and Seljuk periods alongside fossils and ethnographic items.
new.tip: Small enough to see in under an hour.
new.q: Sivas Arkeoloji Müzesi, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Find the tomb of Saint Blaise (Aziz Vlas)
new.desc: The tomb of Saint Blaise, an early Christian bishop of Sebaste (Sivas) revered as a healer of throat and eye ailments, stands in the citadel quarter near the Gök Medrese.
new.tip: The tomb is small; combine it with the Gök Medrese and Abdi Ağa Mansion nearby.
new.q: Aziz Vlas Mezarı, Gök Medrese Mahallesi, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Eat a Sivas breakfast of katmer and pastırma at Taşhan
new.desc: Taşhan is a late-19th-century inn on Atatürk Boulevard that serves a local breakfast of Sivas katmer, antrikot pastırma, kavurma, peskutan, çörek, honey and helva.
new.tip: Go on a weekend morning; pastırma and kavurma are the savoury picks.
new.q: Taşhan, Atatürk Bulvarı No:24, Eskikale, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Eat Sivas köftesi in pide at Köfteci İzzet Usta
new.desc: Sivas köfte is a spiced grilled meatball; here it comes tucked into pide with onion and tomato and is washed down with ayran. İzzet Usta is a locally recommended specialist.
new.tip: Order the köfte in pide with ayran; lunch is the busiest time.
new.q: Köfteci İzzet Usta, Gültepe, Sultan Şehir Bulvarı, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Order kuzu kavurma and pehli at Aşçıbaşı
new.desc: A favourite esnaf lokantası of locals, Aşçıbaşı is known for lamb kavurma, pehli and boiled içli köfte, plus traditional desserts such as kalburabastı and sütlü nuriye.
new.tip: Try the içli köfte and finish with one of the traditional desserts.
new.q: Aşçıbaşı, Gültepe, Erzincan-Erzurum Çevre Yolu No:14, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Eat stone-oven etli pide at Mücahit Etli Pide
new.desc: Mücahit Etli Pide bakes meat-topped Sivas pide in a stone oven and serves it with salad; it is regularly named among the city's best pide spots.
new.tip: Go for lunch and order the etli pide with ayran.
new.q: Mücahit Etli Pide ve Kebap Salonu, Müftülük Sokak 27, Küçükminare, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Try kavun and böğürtlen ice cream at Şahin Pastanesi
new.desc: This long-running Sivas pastry shop is known for ice cream in flavours such as melon (kavun) and blackberry (böğürtlen) alongside plain milk ice cream.
new.tip: Best on summer evenings; try the seasonal fruit flavours.
new.q: Şahin Pastanesi, Kahiroğulları Sokak, Halil Rıfatpaşa, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Try kelle paça and lentil soup at Lezzetçi Çorbacım
new.desc: A soup shop opposite the Meydan Camii in central Sivas, known for its lentil soup, kelle paça and mecimek soups. It keeps regular daily hours.
new.tip: Go early for a hot bowl before a morning in the old town; kelle paça is the traditional Sivas order.
new.q: Lezzetçi Çorbacım, Şemsi Sivasi Caddesi, Çarşıbaşı, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Soak in the hot springs at Sıcak Çermik
new.desc: Sıcak Çermik is a thermal spring area about 30 km from Sivas, with mineral water at 46-50 degrees C used for bathing. A municipal project is expanding its facilities.
new.tip: Check which facilities are open before travelling, as development works are ongoing.
new.q: Sıcak Çermik Kaplıcası, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Visit the İnönü Mansion museum in Sivas
new.desc: A late 19th-century Sivas house bought by the municipality in 1945 and opened as the İnönü Museum. One room and a hall show İsmet İnönü's belongings and photographs, and the building was restored in 2006.
new.tip: The mansion sits on Ali Baba Caddesi in the old centre, an easy walk from the Sivas Congress building. Check opening hours locally.
new.q: İnönü Konağı, Ali Baba Caddesi 18, İnönü Mahallesi, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Ski or hike at Yıldız Dağı
new.desc: The Yıldız Dağı Ski Center in Yakupoğlan village, Yıldızeli, has runs meeting FIS standards for skiing, snowboarding and sledding, with the summit at about 2,552 m. In summer the mountain is used for hiking and camping.
new.tip: The ski season runs roughly December to March; check road and snow conditions first.
new.q: Yakupoğlan, Yıldızeli, Sivas

new.title: Meet Kangal dogs at the Sivas Kangal breeding centre
new.desc: The Sivas Governorship runs a Kangal Dog Production, Training and Protection Centre on the Meraküm hill near Çelebiler village, about 10 km from the city, to protect the genetics of the breed. Sivas is the home province of this Anatolian shepherd.
new.tip: Check visitor rules before going, as access may be restricted.
new.q: Kangal Köpeği Üretim, Eğitim ve Koruma Merkezi, Çelebiler, Merkez, Sivas

new.title: Marvel at the Divriği Great Mosque and Hospital
new.desc: Built in 1228-29 by the Mengujekid dynasty, this mosque and hospital complex was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1985. Its carved portals show thousands of unrepeated motifs, earning it the name Alhambra of Anatolia.
new.tip: Allow time to study the portals; the restoration has finished and the complex is open again.
new.q: Divriği Ulu Camii ve Darüşşifası, Divriği, Sivas

new.title: Bathe with the doctor fish at Kangal Balıklı Kaplıca
new.desc: The Kangal hot spring is home to garra rufa fish that nibble dead skin, and visitors come for psoriasis and other skin conditions. The water is rich in selenium and the facility lies about 13 km from Kangal town.
new.tip: Aimed at multi-day stays in the warm months; follow local medical guidance.
new.q: Kangal Balıklı Kaplıca, Kangal, Sivas

new.title: See the turquoise Gökpınar Lake near Gürün
new.desc: Fed by springs on its bed, Gökpınar is a clear turquoise lake about 20 m deep, nicknamed the natural aquarium. It has been declared a nature park.
new.tip: Respect the protected-area rules; the light is best around midday.
new.q: Gökpınar Gölü, Gürün, Sivas

new.title: Birdwatch at Tödürge Lake near Zara
new.desc: Tödürge Lake, about 5 sq km, is popular with birdwatchers and photographers and is used by rescue teams for under-ice diving training.
new.tip: Visit in spring or autumn for the birds.
new.q: Tödürge Gölü, Zara, Sivas

new.title: Visit Âşık Veysel's house-museum in Sivrialan
new.desc: The poet and saz player Âşık Veysel Şatıroğlu was born in Sivrialan village, Şarkışla. The house he built in 1960 was restored and opened as a museum on 7 December 2012, and his grave lies nearby.
new.tip: Commemorations take place around 21 March, the anniversary of his death.
new.q: Âşık Veysel Müzesi, Sivrialan Köyü, Şarkışla, Sivas

new.title: Explore the Hittite city of Samuha at Kayalıpınar
new.desc: Kayalıpınar near Yıldızeli is the site of the Hittite city of Samuha, an important settlement and cult centre of the Hittite kingdom.
new.tip: This is an excavation site; check access with the Sivas museum before going.
new.q: Kayalıpınar, Yıldızeli, Sivas

new.title: Climb to the Ekinli rock caves near Zara
new.desc: The rocky caves at Ekinli village in Zara district were carved into rock and are thought to have served as hiding places in early Christian times.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes and ask locally for the path.
new.q: Ekinli Köyü, Zara, Sivas

new.title: Stand under the Girlevik Waterfall
new.desc: In Çağlayan, about 35 km from Erzincan, the three-tier Girlevik Waterfall drops from around 40 m. In winter it freezes and attracts ice climbers.
new.tip: Summer is lush; winter brings ice climbing.
new.q: Girlevik Şelalesi, Çağlayan, Erzincan

new.title: Float through the Karanlık Kanyon in Kemaliye
new.desc: The Dark Canyon in the Karasu Valley has walls rising 500-600 m and passages only about 2 m wide. Boat trips, rafting and kayaking run from Kemaliye.
new.tip: Rafting is best in spring; book a local operator in Kemaliye.
new.q: Karanlık Kanyon, Kemaliye, Erzincan

new.title: Walk the Taş Yol rock road above the Euphrates
new.desc: Begun in 1870 and finished in 2002, the Taş Yol is a road of about 8 km with 38 tunnels cut along the Euphrates gorge near Kemaliye.
new.tip: Avoid it in bad weather and watch for traffic in the tunnels.
new.q: Taş Yol, Kemaliye, Erzincan

new.title: Stroll the old Eğin houses of Kemaliye
new.desc: Kemaliye (historic Eğin) has traditional stone and wooden houses with distinctive door knockers; the townscape is on UNESCO's World Heritage Tentative List.
new.tip: Spring is best; try the local sweets lok and gasefe.
new.q: Kemaliye, Erzincan

new.title: Explore the Urartian fortress of Altıntepe
new.desc: Altıntepe near Erzincan has a Urartian temple-palace, a columned reception hall, chamber tombs and a storehouse.
new.tip: Combine it with the Erzincan Museum.
new.q: Altıntepe Ören Yeri, Üzümlü, Erzincan

new.title: Walk the wetlands at Ekşisu
new.desc: Ekşisu is a recreation area about 11 km from Erzincan with naturally carbonated mineral water, around 200 bird species and good air currents for paragliding.
new.tip: Spring and autumn are best for birds.
new.q: Ekşisu Mesire Alanı, Erzincan

new.title: See the round tomb of Mama Hatun in Tercan
new.desc: The late-12th-century Saltukid complex includes a caravanserai, bath, small mosque and a circular-plan tomb. It was restored around 2021.
new.tip: An easy stop on the road towards Erzurum.
new.q: Mama Hatun Külliyesi, Tercan, Erzincan

new.title: Ride the Ergan cable car and ski
new.desc: The Ergan Ski Center, about 17 km from Erzincan, has one of the longest cable car rides in Turkey and ski runs on Ergan Mountain.
new.tip: Ski season is winter; the cable car also gives summer views.
new.q: Ergan Dağı Kayak Merkezi, Erzincan

new.title: Climb to Kemah Castle above the Karasu
new.desc: The cliff-built castle at Kemah was the capital of the Mengücek principality from 1080 to 1228 and has been used since the 2nd-3rd millennium BCE.
new.tip: Check that renovation works are finished before the climb.
new.q: Kemah Kalesi, Kemah, Erzincan

new.title: Visit the Erzincan Museum
new.desc: Opened on 3 May 2023, the 2,030 sq m museum has archaeology and ethnography halls on two floors, with finds from sites such as Altıntepe.
new.tip: Check opening days before going.
new.q: Erzincan Müzesi, Merkez, Erzincan

new.title: Shop for tulum cheese in Erzincan's Bakırcılar Çarşısı
new.desc: The historic coppersmiths' bazaar sells copper work and regional products. Look for the geographically indicated Erzincan tulum cheese, made from Akkaraman sheep and goat milk and aged 3-4 months.
new.tip: Look for the GI label, as imitations are sold.
new.q: Bakırcılar Çarşısı, Cumhuriyet Meydanı, Merkez, Erzincan

new.title: Try Erzincan yaprak döner at Evin Döner
new.desc: Erzincan is known for its döner, made with meat from high-pasture animals. Evin Döner on 13 Şubat Caddesi is a named local spot where reviewers praise the döner.
new.tip: Service can be slow at busy times.
new.q: Evin Döner, Kızılay Mahallesi, 13 Şubat Caddesi No:1, Merkez, Erzincan

new.title: Have an Erzincan breakfast at Simay Restaurant
new.desc: Simay Restaurant on Halit Paşa Caddesi in Erzincan serves meze, grills, desserts and an open-buffet breakfast, with delivery available.
new.tip: Come for the breakfast buffet and try tulum cheese alongside it.
new.q: Simay Restaurant, Halit Paşa Caddesi, Merkez, Erzincan

new.title: See the single-arch Acemoğlu Bridge on the Karasu
new.desc: A single-arch cut-stone bridge across the Acemoğlu Strait on the Karasu River near Kemah, protected since 1980.
new.tip: A short stop on the Kemah road.
new.q: Acemoğlu Köprüsü, Kemah, Erzincan

new.title: Find the surviving gate of Erzincan Castle
new.desc: The Kale Kapısı in Beybağı quarter is the only fully intact part of the old Erzincan castle. About 30 m west lie the ruins of a stone tower thought to be the inner keep.
new.tip: A short stop in the city centre; combine it with the Erzincan Museum.
new.q: Erzincan Kale Kapısı, Beybağı Mahallesi, Merkez, Erzincan
